# SATU Collection
URL: https://another-life.dk/collection.html

Collection
The SATU collection.
Satu means one in Indonesian. One material, one system, one idea carried through every piece. The collection is made from repurposed teak, timber that has already lived a life, often in old joglo houses, and given another through Danish design and Indonesian hands.
01The ChairDining rooms, restaurants and terracesL 45 × W 45 × H 80 cm · Seat 45 cm02The Sun LoungerPoolside and outdoorsL 211 × W 75 × H 32 cm03The BenchDining tables, terraces and hallsL 206 × W 45 × H 45 cm04The Lounge ChairLounges, lobbies and terracesL 75 × W 75 × H 67 cm · Seat 32 cm05The Side TablePoolside, terraces and loungesL 45 × W 45 × H 45 cm06The Coffee TableLounges, lobbies and terracesL 100 × W 75 × H 32 cm07The TableDining rooms and restaurantsL 220 × W 100 × H 75 cm
About SATUOld wood, new purpose, long life.
Every piece is modular and knock-down. It travels flat, comes apart without damage, and goes back together as it was. If one part reaches its end, only that part is changed.
The surface is finished with Shou Sugi Ban: the teak is darkened with flame and finished with natural oil. What is left is the material itself: honest, tactile, and made to age well.
Shared by every pieceOne design. Different lives.
Material
Repurposed teak
Finish
Shou Sugi Ban. Flame-darkened, natural oil.
Construction
Modular, knock-down, replaceable parts
Shipping
Flat-packed. Assembled on site.
Made in
Indonesia
Pricing
On request. Ex works, Indonesia

# The Chair — SATU
URL: https://another-life.dk/the-chair.html

SATU · 01 / 07
The Chair
A knock-down dining chair in repurposed teak. It travels flat, goes together on site and is designed to be repaired for decades rather than replaced.

Price
On request. Ex works, Indonesia
Shipping
Flat-packed, assembled on site
Enquire about The Chair
DetailsAbout The Chair.
The first piece we designed, and the one the rest of SATU grew from.
The bolts are part of the look. Three-bolt clusters at the seat and leg joints hold the frame and let it be taken apart again.
Every component can be replaced on its own. A broken leg is a new leg, not a new chair.
Like every Another Life piece, it is made from timber that already had a first life. Marks from that life stay visible, wherever they don't reduce strength. And if a part ever wears out: replace the part, not the piece.
In detail
Another Life PassportIts own story, one scan away.
Each piece carries a QR code that opens its own story: where the wood of The Chair lived before, who made it, and how to care for it and repair it.

# Another Life Mission
URL: https://another-life.dk/mission.html

The best day was yesterday. Let's make sure there's a tomorrow.
Mission
On this page
Why we exist · Design · Where we're heading
PurposeWhy we exist.
To make furniture that lasts a long time.
Hotels and restaurants spend years building a sense of place, and many of them look to Danish design for credibility. Then they furnish those places with pieces that won't last: plastic chairs and loungers that are bought, worn out and replaced on a short cycle.
That gap is the reason Another Life exists. We make furniture that earns the design it borrows from: well made, built from material that already exists, and designed to be repaired rather than thrown away.
The new luxury is longevity.
Design principlesDanish design, made where the material is.
Our design follows a Scandinavian tradition: simple, functional, made to last and to never go out of style. The pieces are made by hand in Indonesia, close to the timber and the people who work it.
Sketches, drawings and a burned sample on the design table.
Knock-down
Every piece ships disassembled and bolts together on site. Flat furniture takes far less space to move than assembled furniture.
Reassemblable
Joints must survive being taken apart and put back together many times, not once. A hotel can move, store or reconfigure its furniture.
Modular
Each component can be replaced on its own. One design can take different materials and parts over time, like a system rather than a single object.
Honest material
Grain, age, marks and imperfections stay visible. We want each piece to look like it has a story.
Where we're headingGive back. Collaborate.
We're just getting started, and we have big plans. We haven't planted a forest yet, and we won't pretend we have. But here's where we're heading.
Give back
We want to share what we build with the communities behind our furniture: the makers we work with and the places the wood comes from.
Work with us

---

# Material and Making
URL: https://another-life.dk/material.html

Material and making
Timber that already lived once.
Where our wood comes from, how we burn and oil it, and how every piece is built.
On this page
Where our wood comes from · Shou Sugi Ban, our way · Making · Hardware · Shipping
Chapter 1 · Where our wood comes from17,000 islands, built in wood.
Indonesia has more than 17,000 islands, and for centuries much of it was built in wood.
Today many of them are making way for concrete. The teak inside is often older than our grandparents. Throw it away? Not on our watch. We'd rather give it another life.
Our teak is repurposed: timber that has already lived a life, often in old joglo houses, and also in bridges, boats and other structures. Each piece's own story can be traced through the Passport.
Old posts and beams, marked and sorted before they are cut.
Reclaimed? Not always.Ask where it stood.
“Reclaimed” is one of the easiest words to put on a label, and one of the hardest to check. It matters, because a new tree is never just one tree.
And teak?New teak isn’t old teak.
Most new teak in Indonesia is grown in plantations, and some of it is cut very young. A 2018 study compared 10-year-old plantation teak with 40-year-old teak:
Heartwood, the durable core
10 years≈ 40%
40 years≈ 80%
The young wood was also less resistant to rot. The teak in an old joglo grew slowly, often for many decades, before it was ever cut. That kind of teak is no longer easy to buy new. Reclaiming it is how we work with it.
Source: Rizanti et al., Comparison of teak wood properties: short versus long rotation, Annals of Forest Science 2018
Chapter 2 · Shou Sugi Ban, our wayFire, borrowed from Japan.
Burning the surface of the timber.
In Japan, carpenters have protected wood by setting it on fire for centuries. Really. It's called yakisugi, and a charred surface helps wood stand up to weather and bugs.
We borrowed the idea and tried it on something harder: repurposed teak. We burn the surface, then rub in natural oil. The idea is to help the wood handle the sun and almost any weather.
An old Japanese technique, moved to a hard wood.
MakingMade in Indonesia.
Every piece is made by hand in Indonesia by makers we work with directly, in small batches.
Producing close to the material keeps the supply chain short and visible.
Stacks of repurposed teak, drilled one board at a time.
The hardwareBolts built to outlive the chair.
Three dots. One circle.
Hardware is usually the last thing anyone thinks about. It is often the cheapest part of a piece of furniture, and the first to fail: screws rust, threads strip, and a good chair is thrown out because of a part that cost almost nothing.
We turned that around. Every SATU joint is held by engineered stainless steel (SUS) bolts that screw into threaded inserts set into the wood. The bolt can be opened and closed again and again without wearing out.
The three-bolt clusters you see on every piece aren't decoration. They hold everything together, and they're designed to last longer than the furniture around them.
They also carry the idea behind the name. Each bolt stands for a life the piece can have, and together they form the letter A, for ANOTHER — LIFE.
ShippingStop shipping air.
An assembled chair is mostly empty space: between the legs, under the seat, behind the backrest. Ship it like that and you pay to move air across the ocean.
Flat-packed, a 40 ft high-cube container holds around 1,300 of our chairs, against roughly 350 assembled. Almost four times as many chairs per trip, so fewer containers, less fuel and a lower cost for every chair.
Our estimates. The final figures depend on packaging and loading.
20 ft40 ft high-cube
Flat-packed · ~1,300Assembled · ~350
Drag the slider to compare. Illustration.

# Another Life Passport
URL: https://another-life.dk/passport.html

Another Life Passport
A story you can scan.
A system that gives every piece its own story: from the life its wood lived before, to every life it lives next.
One small code on the furniture. One page behind it. A story that keeps growing as the piece is used, repaired and passed on.
How it worksFrom one code to a whole story.
We don't believe one label can tell the whole story. A certification can tell you where a material comes from.
Certifications have their place. But we've learned that a stamp of approval doesn't always mean a product is truly sustainable, and we believe sustainability should go much further than meeting a set of requirements.
That's what the Passport is for: showing the evidence, piece by piece, instead of asking you to trust a stamp.
01 / 05
01MarkedOne code on every piece.
The system creates a batch code and a QR code, ready for the engraver. The code under the QR is a backup anyone can type in.
02ScannedA guest points a phone at it.
No app. The camera opens the page for that piece, with the batch code at the top.
03Its livesThe whole story in a minute.
From a teak tree, to the house, bridge or boat it held up, to the workshop, to the room it stands in now.
04Its journeyHow far it travelled.
Its route from the workshop, step by step, with an estimate of the transport CO₂ for that piece.
05Its careSomething loose? Tell us.
A short form with a photo comes straight to us, so a small repair keeps the piece in use.
Try itScan the code at the top of this page, or open the example.
Open the example passportFind a piece by its code
For hospitalityA story guests can read for themselves.
Hotels and restaurants are asked more and more what their spaces are made of, and furniture is often left out. The Passport is designed to give every piece a traceable origin, with something real behind it.
And it starts conversations. A guest scans a chair and reads that its wood once held up a family home.

# For Hospitality
URL: https://another-life.dk/hospitality.html

For hospitality
Furniture that outlasts the fit-out.
The Chair in a restaurant above the forest.
We make furniture for places that host people: boutique hotels, resorts, restaurants and cafés.
Who we work withThe people who shape a place.
We like to work directly with owners and the people who define what a hospitality brand stands for, not only how it looks. If your place is built on values, your furniture should carry them.
We also work with the architects and interior designers who specify furniture for hotels and restaurants.
Choosing Another Life is a way to adopt better decisions without building the supply chain yourself. The story comes with the piece.

# Another Life Questions
URL: https://another-life.dk/faq.html

Questions
Questions, answered plainly.
What is Another Life?
Another Life is a hospitality furniture brand. We make furniture from repurposed teak, designed in a Danish tradition, shipped flat and built to be kept for a very long time.
What does the name mean?
The teak we use has already lived one life, in a house, a bridge or a boat. Every piece we make from it is meant to keep going: repaired, moved and handed on to its next owner.
What is SATU?
SATU is our first collection. The name is the Indonesian word for one, because every piece shares the same wood, finish and way of building.
What is the furniture made from?
Repurposed teak: timber that has already lived a life, often in old joglo houses. We give it another life through Danish design and Indonesian hands.
What is Shou Sugi Ban?
Shou Sugi Ban, or yakisugi in Japanese, is a centuries-old technique of charring wood with flame. In Japan it was made for cedar, a softwood. We use it on a hardwood, repurposed teak: we burn the surface, then finish it with natural oil. The result is a deep black colour and a texture you can feel.
Why do you burn a hardwood?
Because we wanted to see what an old Japanese idea could do for teak to protect it. Charring gives the surface a protective, characterful skin, and the idea is to help the wood handle strong sun. We finish it with natural oil, which soaks into the wood instead of sitting on top as a coating.
What is a joglo?
A joglo is a traditional Javanese house: a tall roof carried by four big teak pillars, put together with joinery so it can be taken apart and moved. Many old joglos are making way for concrete houses. Much of the teak we use comes from houses like these.
Why does every piece look a little different?
Because the teak has a history. Marks and nail holes from the wood's first life are part of its character, and we keep them visible as a quiet record of where it has been. Strength always comes first, so each piece is built to last.
Is Another Life furniture sustainable?
Sustainability guides every decision we make: repurposed teak, a flame-darkened finish with natural oil, flat-pack shipping, and furniture designed to be repaired rather than replaced. We believe the most sustainable piece is the one you keep for decades, so that is what we make.
How do you show where the wood comes from?
Through the story of our wood: old houses, bridges and boats across Indonesia. Every piece also carries the Another Life Passport, a QR code that opens its own story, from its first life to its next.
What happens when a hotel no longer needs the furniture?
It comes apart. Undo the bolts and every piece packs flat, can be stored, and goes back together for its next place or owner. If a part is worn, you replace that part, not the piece. Our furniture is made to be used, never stacked in a corner, and never sent to landfill.
Is the furniture recyclable?
It is solid wood finished with natural oil, so at the very end of its life it can be. But we hope it never gets there. Recycling ends a product's life and takes energy to make something new. We would rather a piece is kept, repaired, moved and passed on, like a glass bottle that is refilled instead of melted down.
Do you plant trees?
It is part of our mission. We want to plant new trees for the wood we use, give back to the communities and makers behind our furniture, and do it with partners who care about the same things. We have just started, so we say it as a goal, not as something we already do. If you run a planting or community project, we would love to hear from you.
Can the furniture be used outdoors?
Yes. It is made for hospitality spaces indoors and out, from dining rooms and lobbies to pools, terraces and gardens.
How is the furniture shipped?
Flat-packed. Every piece travels knocked down, so more fits in each container, and it is bolted together on site.
What holds the furniture together?
Stainless steel bolts, three at every main joint, screwed into threaded inserts in the wood. Hardware is often the weakest, cheapest part of furniture. We made it one of the strongest, so the joints can be taken apart and tightened again for decades.
Can the furniture be repaired?
Yes, and that is the heart of the design. Parts are bolted together, so any single part can be replaced and the piece goes straight back into service. It can be taken apart and put back together again and again.
What is the Another Life Passport?
Our QR tracing system. A small QR code on the furniture opens the story of that piece: where its wood came from and what it was before, who made it, how it travelled, and how to care for it and repair it. When a piece moves to a new owner, its story moves with it. No app is needed.
Who do you make furniture for?
Boutique hotels, resorts, restaurants and cafés, and the architects and interior designers who work with them. We love working with the people who shape what a place stands for.
Is Another Life Danish?
Yes. Another Life is Danish-designed, rooted in the Danish and Scandinavian design tradition. We are Danish at heart and inspired by the world. Every piece is made by hand in Indonesia, close to the material and the makers.
How do I order?
Send us a message with your space, the pieces you like and your timeline. We will reply with options, pricing and lead times.
